hook: The grayscale trick works. But not for the reason you think.
topic: Why grayscale reduces phone use and what it reveals about visual reward cues
body:
**The grayscale trick works. But not for the reason you think.**

Turning your phone screen to grayscale reduces usage for most people who try it. The common explanation is that colour is stimulating and removing it makes the phone less appealing. That is partially true. But the more precise mechanism is different.

The bright, saturated colours in app interfaces — the red notification badge, the blue of Twitter, the gradient of Instagram Stories — are not just aesthetic choices. They are visual reward cues. They signal: there is something here worth checking. They trigger the approach response before you have evaluated whether there is actually anything there.

Grayscale removes the signal, not the content. And without the signal, the automatic reach is slower to fire. There is a half-second gap where the reflex does not launch immediately — and in that half-second, your prefrontal cortex can engage.

Half a second of friction is not much. But it is enough to interrupt automaticity. And interrupting automaticity is the first structural move in the entire protocol.

Grayscale is not a solution. It is a first layer. But layers compound, and this one costs you nothing to implement tonight.

Settings, accessibility, colour filters, grayscale. Do it before you go to sleep.

Full layered system in the link in bio.
